newsitem.title: CANADA: Sable gas backers say delays threaten project.
newsitem.headline: Sable gas backers say delays threaten project.

text.p: A battle between pipeline companies aiming to ship natural gas from Sable Island off Canada's east coast heated up again on Monday when the Sable backers said regulatory delays could jeopardize the development.

"(Sable Offshore Energy Project) has been clear about project dates and timetable for almost three years now," Ken Miller, vice-present of frontier for project proponent Mobil Oil Canada, said in a statement.

Miller made the comment in response to an anouncement on Friday by Trans Quebec & Maritimes, a firm owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP, that it will sumbit its proposal to Canada's National Energy Board in August.
TQM is competing with Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, owned by Mobil, Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp.

Maritimes & Northeast would move the estimated 480 million cubic feet of gas per day to Northeast U.S. markets from Nova Scotia through New Brunswick. The TQM expansion would also move the gas to Boston, but via Quebec.
Miller said TQM knew about the Sable and Maritimes & Northeast proposals since 1995 and indicated early last year that it would file a development application.
"The Joint Review Panel and the government have clearly stated that other projects will be provided separate regulatory processes and we support this," Miller said.
"It is hard for us to view TQM's proposal as anything other than a late attempt at delay in order to provide them time to catch up."
He said the Sable developers expected to plan the project diligently at each stage in order to build credibility and justify the investments.
The Sable Island gas project and Maritimes & Northeast pipeline were estimated to cost a total of C$3 billion.
"If we do not have that certainty then the risks inherent in the project may at some point become too great," Miller said.
Partners in the Sable project, which would see development of six gas fields off Nova Scotia, include Mobil, Shell Canada Ltd, Imperial Oil Ltd and Nova Scotia Resources Ltd.
